evidence: createApp registers Express routes (app.get/app.post), and each handler hands the work to a FulfilmentService method (listProducts, addProduct, placeOrder, transition, cancelOrder). This is transport adapter work.
The POST /products and POST /orders handlers only check the type and shape of the request body (typeof checks). This is input parsing, not business rules.
The response mapping { id: p.id, name: p.name, stock: p.stock } is an HTTP response format.
The error middleware maps DomainError.kind to HTTP status through STATUS, and SyntaxError to 400. This is HTTP error translation.
GET /orders checks the state filter with the domain's isOrderState instead of re-implementing order-state knowledge.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts is an Express HTTP adapter, and that work belongs in the infrastructure layer. It does four things: it maps routes to service calls, checks the shape and type of request bodies and query parameters, maps domain objects to response bodies, and turns errors into HTTP status codes. It contains no business rules. Stock checks, order state-transition rules and order placement logic all live behind FulfilmentService. The query state is checked with the domain's isOrderState instead of being re-implemented here. The transitions array only decides which application operations get a route. The file throws DomainError('validation') for malformed input. That reuses a domain type but stays transport validation. No responsibility from another layer kind is present.
